$comment: The contract cases of API v1. The site REPLAYS each one (tests/Feature/ApiContractTest.php: build `setup`, send `request`, compare `response`); the mod READS each response body (Core.Checks: feed `response.body` to the reader named in `read`, compare what it derives); check-spec.py holds every request and response body to openapi.json. One file, three executors — see spec/README.md.

conventions.setup: A fixture name from `fixtures`, or an inline object of the same shape: users {ref: {name, deleted?, banned?}}, games {ref: {name, slug, steam_id?}}, translations {ref: {game, user, uuid, visibility, parent?, status?, accepts_branches?, notes?, resources_url?, file_hash, lines, vote_count?}}, votes [{user, translation, value}]. The site creates the rows; the mod ignores it.
conventions.request: {method, path, as?, query?, headers?, body?, body_encoding?}. `as` names a user of the setup: the site sends a fresh token of theirs. `{{a.b.c}}` in path, query and header strings is a setup value (`translations.main.id`) or a `capture` of the prelude. In a body, {"$ref": "translations.main.id"} is the same thing as a JSON value and {"$json": {...}} is that object serialised as a string (the upload's `content`).
conventions.prelude: Requests sent before the one under test, in order; `capture: {name: "header:ETag" | "body:token"}` keeps a value for `{{name}}`. Site only.
conventions.request_valid: false when the request body is one the route must REFUSE: check-spec.py then requires the schema to refuse it too.
conventions.response: {status, headers?, body?}. Objects match PARTIALLY (keys named must match, others are not looked at); arrays match exactly in length, element by element. Matchers: {"$is": "integer" | "number" | "string" | "boolean" | "iso8601" | "file_hash" | "session_key" | "url" | "any"}, {"$ref": ...} (the setup value), {"$contains": "text"}, {"$absent": true} (the key must NOT be there). Both executors resolve these the same way; the mod resolves a `$ref` to a stable number of its own.
conventions.read: {reader, expects}: which reader of the mod's ApiReaders takes this body, and the values it must derive, as dotted paths of the result (`Vote.CanVote`). Absent when the mod does not read this route.

cases.why: the branch is a proposal between two people, never a catalogue entry: one row, and the per-game group says the same
a loose name touches several games on purpose; the answer names each, and the client keeps the group it asked about (GameNames.Which picks the exact one)
without a game there is no 'per game' to be complete about, and a shape that implied it would be a lie
the arrow is coloured when the panel opens, not after a second click that would withdraw the vote
an entry that found nothing still answers, in its place: a missing key would read as 'not asked', which a caller cannot tell from 'nothing exists'
nothing exists: an upload would create a new Main
the Main learns what its contributions HOLD, not how many people took the file: one branch, one new hand-written line to review
a contributor learns what THEIR contribution holds and whether its Main is still there; what other contributors do is none of their business
told BEFORE the click, to the one person it is for: an upload would become her branch, and the Main takes them
a client that reads false stops offering Contribute instead of letting somebody find out on the click
the Main closed since: nothing more can be done with this row as a branch, and the one way on is a fork
a branch of nothing: the mod used to keep saying 'you are a branch' long after there was anything to be a branch of
where an account stands is a question only an account can ask
check-uuid and check in one payload, as the sync stream's `state` event carries it; `branches_pending_review` is `branches_with_work`, deliberately
absent, never zero: a client that asked not to be told has not been told there is nothing
the player holding somebody else's file — the one person who most needs to know whether they may send corrections back — is told at the top level
the one call somebody with no account can make about the file they installed; without `uploader` the mod could only call the work 'Website'
the validator covers the vote count and the uploader too, so a 304 really means nothing the caller could see has moved — and the caller keeps every value it has

body.message: A branch is visible to whoever wrote it, and to the Main owner for merging

cases.why: a proposal between two people; the API must not describe what it will not serve
its author, always — a contributor who could not ask whether their own branch changed would be told nothing about work they wrote
the file itself, fingerprinted by its ETag; a copy held with that hash is the published one
the mod sends the hash it holds, quoted, and is spared the body
same single definition as check: isReadableBy
ordered on the content date, which a vote or a download does not move

body.message: You are not the Main owner of this translation

cases.why: what the other contributions carry is not a contributor's business
a uuid nobody has published: the sender becomes the Main of a new lineage and the file records id and hash as `_source`
an update keeps the row and its languages whatever the request says about them — here a pair that would be refused on a new translation
nobody writes on somebody else's row: an upload into a lineage one does not lead becomes one's own branch of it

body.error: This translation does not accept contributions. Your lines are safe: use Fork in the mod to publish your own version of it instead.

expects.Error: This translation does not accept contributions. Your lines are safe: use Fork in the mod to publish your own version of it instead.

cases.why: a refusal is a refusal, never a quiet substitution: turning it into a fork would change the file's uuid from a server that cannot see that file

error.$contains: The account that owned this translation has been deleted

cases.why: the Main is still there and still says it accepts branches; nobody will ever read one, and a contribution nobody can merge is a refusal that takes months to notice

error.$contains: has been removed by its author

cases.why: a lineage that lost its head is not a new translation: the next upload must not take it over, inheriting a following it never earned

a Main who closes must stop receiving updates from every branch already in place — and the contributor is told THEIR branch is frozen, not merely that the Main takes none. This door stood after determineOwnership, which refused first with the generic sentence; the case found it unreachable

error.$contains: identical to a translation already published by @alice

cases.why: the same lines under another uuid publish one person's work under another's name; the author is named only because her row is public

body.error: Invalid translation format: 1 entries have errors

expects.Error: Invalid translation format: 1 entries have errors

cases.why: the bare form is still READ by the mod but refused at the door: every published line is `{v, t}`

body.error: Source and target languages must be different.

cases.why: on a NEW translation the pair is checked; on an update or a branch it is ignored
a name, never a code: Laravel's validation body, whose `errors` the mod joins into one sentence
every client we ship compresses its POST bodies: `Content-Encoding: gzip`, inflated by the site before validation
a GET carries no body worth decompressing; refusing the header is what keeps the decoder unreachable from every route
only what was sent is written, and the content date does not move: a better wording is not a release

body.message: A contribution inherits whether it is finished from the translation it contributes to.

expects.Error: A contribution inherits whether it is finished from the translation it contributes to.

cases.why: refused rather than ignored: answering 200 to a request that changed nothing would teach a client that it had

body.message: This translation belongs to somebody else.

cases.why: one writes on one's own row and nowhere else; the admin path stays in /admin
the answer carries the caller's own vote so the arrow can be drawn without asking again
one gesture, both ways; null is 'no vote', which the client draws as a neutral arrow

body.message: You cannot vote on this translation

cases.why: whether a caller MAY vote is the server's rule; `vote.can_vote` says it before the click
games holding a published translation, and only those: a branch is neither counted nor listed
only `status: complete` rows reach this listing — the second game's is in progress, so it lists nothing and no language
the catalogue before any external quota; a game already known is answered without a store call
`access_code` is what the Linked devices screen calls this line; without it nobody could tell which access is theirs
the one 403 a client reads as 'sign out': `error` is exactly `Account banned`
a whole library in one call, with what waits on each row — fifty calls to check-uuid would starve the account's budget
null on the side the question does not apply to — 'not a branch' is not 'fine', and 'not a Main' is not 'nothing waits'

text.$contains: contribution(s) to review on your Sample Game translation (French)

cases.why: pre-rendered English for an overlay, with the page that answers it
no ids: everything unread
the token never comes back through this API: it arrives once over the SSE stream named by `device_code`
every mod already installed calls this with an empty body, and none of them will ever be updated
revokes the token presented and no other
giving up a credential is not a privilege; this route sits outside the ban check on purpose
destination server by default: the arbitrated result becomes the published translation, so only its owner may open it

body.error: You can only merge preview your own translations.

expects.Error: You can only merge preview your own translations.

cases.why: ownership is what publishing requires
a comparison whose result only goes back to the game writes nothing here, so a branch may measure itself against its Main
one channel: the file holds what the player sent until the page replaces it with what they decided, and a client collects it only after the stream's `merge_completed` event

body.error: Merge result not found or expired.

expects.Error: Merge result not found or expired.

cases.why: unknown, expired or somebody else's: one answer, so a leaked token learns nothing

body.error: This comparison was published; download the translation instead.

cases.why: a published comparison became the online version and is read back through the ordinary download
the mod loaded another translation; the page learns it over its own stream
anonymous by design: the 64-character mod key is the whole credential, and it never reaches a browser
a few dozen bytes: the file is fetched only once the hash says it is worth fetching
the browser picks it up on its next state poll; the answer carries browser presence so the holder can conclude the page was closed
verbatim, metadata included: it replaces translations.json, so `_uuid` and `_source` must survive the round trip
a proposal, staged under the page's own Save; nothing is written on the holder's side
a session ends when the page is closed or the holder stops, never on a timer; the TTL is a backstop for orphans
idempotent: an already-gone session is a success for the caller

body.error: Edit session expired or not found.

cases.why: the client forgets the session; a network failure is NOT this and keeps a resumable session on disk
`holder` is a closed word: game or manager; it decides what a human is shown, so an invented one is refused rather than filed as the mod
